question.:question/problem:
Calculate $ABC$, where $$ A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -6\end{bmatrix},\,C=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}. $$
$ABC=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 1$ matrix, and $C$ is a $1\times 3$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $1\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding only $1$ entry, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $2\times 3$ matrix, which will require finding $6$ entries.

So, we find the product $AB$ first: 

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -6\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0\cdot 4+(-3)\cdot (-6)\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0+18\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}18\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $(AB)$ by $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =(AB)\,C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}18\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}54 & 0 & 72\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
